sources.title: Network meta-analysis of CDK4/6 inhibitors. Scientific Reports, February 2024
sources.used_for: Seven phase III trials, 4,415 patients. No significant pairwise overall-survival difference between the three drugs. Its Table 1 lists MONARCH 3 at HR 0.804 (0.637-1.015) and its “Year of updated data” row gives 2023 for that trial, and its reference list cites the SABCS 2023 final overall-survival abstract — so its MONARCH 3 input is the FINAL analysis, not the interim HR 0.754. An earlier version of this page said the opposite, on the strength of our own automated check rather than the paper; an outside reviewer opened the table and corrected us (CORR-01 era). Median follow-up: the abstract gives 73.3 months (range 48.7-97.2), the results section gives 70.2 over the same range. The page prints the abstract's and discloses the discrepancy, which is the source's own; see CORR-08.

sources.title: Shaaban MHA, Elbaiomy MA, Eltantawy A, Abdel-Fattah A-HE, Shamaa SSA (2024) — Comparing ribociclib versus palbociclib as a second line treatment in combination with fulvestrant in metastatic breast cancer: a randomized clinical trial. Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Prevention 25(9), 3039-3049.
sources.used_for: A randomised, open-label phase III trial putting two of these three drugs directly against each other, 1:1, registered NCT05670054, at the Oncology Centre Mansoura University, Egypt, July 2022 to December 2023. 116 patients, 58 per arm, randomised “using 29 blocks with block size of four” by opaque sealed envelope. Clinical benefit at six months 58.6% in both arms (34 of 58 either way); median progression-free survival 13.67 months on palbociclib against 12.69 on ribociclib, not significantly different. Conclusion: “Both Ribociclib and palbociclib have similar CBR, PFS and toxicity profile.” Overall survival was immature and median OS was not calculated.
sources.WHY_THIS_MATTERS: This page verified that NCCN says the CDK4/6 inhibitors have not been directly compared, and then printed that as an unscoped claim about the world, four times. This trial is why that was wrong. It was found by the counterexample role, whose only instruction is to break the page's universal negatives; eighteen fact-check runs and an outside review had passed over the sentence.

sources.endpoint_note: PRIMARY objectives are clinical benefit rate, quality of life and toxicity. Progression-free survival and overall survival are SECONDARY. The sample size was calculated on overall response rate (58 per group at 80% power). The page now says so where it prints the PFS figures.
sources.ENDPOINT_DISCREPANCY: The paper names one primary endpoint and powers on another. Its Introduction: “The primary objectives are to compare the clinical benefit rate (CBR), quality of life and toxicity profiles... Secondary objectives were assessment of Progression free survival and Overall survival.” Its Sample size calculation: “The primary outcome of interest is the overall response rate (ORR)”, sized from ORR 55% (MONALEESA-2) against 25% (PALOMA-3), alpha 5%, power 80%. CBR counts stable disease and ORR does not, so these are different endpoints. The page prints both because the source states both. Same shape as the network meta-analysis printing 73.3 and 70.2.

sources.title: Tanguy M-L, Cabel L, Berger F, Pierga J-Y, Savignoni A, Bidard F-C. Cdk4/6 inhibitors and overall survival: power of first-line trials in metastatic breast cancer. npj Breast Cancer 4:14 (2018).
sources.used_for: What the paper ACTUALLY establishes, now that it has been read in full: the statistical power of PALOMA-2, MONALEESA-2, MONALEESA-7 and MONARCH-3 to reach significance on overall survival, computed with Freedman's formula at a two-sided 5% type I error. “PALOMA-2 and MONALEESA trials have an almost similar power despite different allocation ratios, while MONARCH-3 has a more limited power.” All four are under 70% power unless the median OS gain exceeds twelve months. Its conclusion: “if a significant OS improvement is observed in some but not at all trials, this discrepancy might be more attributable to chance than to a truly different drug efficacy.” It also records that MONARCH-3's main OS analysis was planned as part of a pooled analysis with MONARCH-2, so “OS analyses of MONARCH-3 as a single study could be reported as exploratory analyses with no prespecified maturity”.
sources.WHAT_IT_DOES_NOT_SAY: ANYTHING ABOUT CONFIDENCE INTERVAL WIDTH. The paper computes power to reach significance and nothing else. Both this page and the announcement email attributed to it the observation that an interval's width follows from what a trial was powered to detect. That observation is ours. The misattribution was live from 28 August to 1 September, and was found by the fact-check gate on the email, not on the page — the page's version was better hidden, because it attached our observation to their names and then described their real argument correctly in the next clause.
sources.declared_interests: “F.-C. Bidard is part of advisory boards and received research grants (unrelated to this study) from Pfizer, Novartis, and Lilly. Other authors have no competing interest.” Recorded because this page runs a disclosure-symmetry argument about P-VERIFY and PALMARES-2, and a source it leans on for the power argument carries the same entanglement. Funded by Institut Curie SIRIC 2, grant INCa-DGOS-Inserm_12554.

sources.title: Corrigendum to “Abemaciclib plus a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor as initial therapy for HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer: final overall survival results of MONARCH 3”. Ann Oncol, 2025;36:1556
sources.used_for: The record that MONARCH 3's final overall-survival paper was formally corrected in December 2025, and that the correction does not touch any figure this page prints. The corrigendum's whole content is one error in Figure 4: in the placebo plus NSAI arm of the CHEMOTHERAPY-FREE SURVIVAL analysis, the number of events was published as 162 and is 132. Chemotherapy-free survival is an exploratory endpoint and appears nowhere on this page. The overall-survival results, the hazard ratio, the P value, the alpha-spending description and the follow-up duration are unaffected.

access.note:
THIS ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE OF A FIELD IN A BIBLIOGRAPHIC RECORD. On 2026-09-01 the operator pasted PubMed's MEDLINE record for S003 while asking whether similar and citing articles were worth reviewing. Its EIN field read: Ann Oncol. 2025 Dec;36(12):1556. This page had been printing six figures from a paper that had been formally corrected, and nothing in this repository knew.

An erratum is the one class of secondary document that can silently falsify a figure already published. It is also mechanically detectable: every MEDLINE record carries EIN and CIN fields. Checking them is free and requires no judgement, and not checking them is how a correction notice sits unread for nine months.

What it says is now known and it is narrow. Read in full, the notice corrects one number in one figure of an exploratory endpoint this page does not use. That is a real answer rather than an assumed one: the document was obtained and read, and the claim that it does not affect us rests on the notice itself and not on its title.
